messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH severity alert fired for service=runtime-inference - 'p99 latency > 750ms (5m)'. Triggered policy=latency-p99-prod. PD link <https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD1234>
Jamie: Acked. I'm on it. Can someone grab traces/dash and confirm customer impact? :white_check_mark:
Riley: On it — looking at latency heatmap now. Spike concentrated in us-west-2, Route name=/v1/generate, tail latency only. No increase in 5xx. Might be KV cache churn or an autoscale jitter.
Priya: I see the same. Per-route qps stable. KV cache hit rate dropped ~35% around 12:03 UTC. Correlates with a small burst of new deployments earlier (canary batch).
Carlos: Re: deployments — deploy-bot shows two canaries finished at 11:58 and 12:01. Both to the runtime pool in us-west-2. No errors reported.
Jamie: Good catch. Priya can you try warming KV caches on a sample router? Riley, can you pull the top traces and check where time is being spent (KV get vs attention compute)?
Priya: Running warmup on router-17: `curl -s -X POST https://internal/kv/warmup -d '{"prefix":"/v1/generate"}'` — kicking now. ETA 30s.
Riley: Top traces show ~60% extra time in KV lookup latency (median +120ms) and increased queueing in the router when prefix misses happen.
Jamie: Sounds like transient KV coldstart after the canary. Carlos, any capacity events or GCE preemptions in us-west-2 around that time?
Carlos: No preemptions. GPU utilization steady. Network perf normal. Only signal is the KV miss spike. Could be a metadata sync lag after canary nodes joined.
incident-bot: :info: Alert note: Automatic suppression attempted at 12:06 UTC (policy=auto-suppression-low-impact). Suppression deferred because p99 > threshold for >2m.
Jamie: We'll keep monitoring. Priya — any sign that customers are seeing errors or degraded UX? Support queue?
Priya: Support shows one DM from customer-team-alpha about a slow response on a heavy prompt at 12:05, but no escalations. No broad customer-facing errors.
Riley: Warmup completed on router-17; KV hit rate recovering. I'll patch a temporary bypass to prefer local in-memory fallback for prefix cache for 5m, rolling to 3 routers.
Jamie: Go ahead. Patch command? Paste the command here.
Riley: `kubectl -n runtime exec -it router-17 -- /bin/sh -c "echo 'enable_local_prefix_cache=1' > /etc/runtime/flags/local_cache && kill -HUP 1"`
Carlos: Rolling the bypass now to router-17, 18, 19. Observability: qps stays same; latency dropping in p95/p99 as cache warms.
Jamie: Noted. I'm going to hand off to the next on-call in 25m. If this resolves and auto-clears, we'll mark as no major customer impact. Priya, please keep watch on support.
incident-bot: :thumbsup: Jamie acknowledged handoff scheduled for 12:30 UTC. Next on-call: Priya.
Priya: Taking point. Will escalate to infra if KV miss rate doesn't drop below 5% in 10m.
Riley: p99 down to ~420ms after bypass and warmup. KV hit rate back to 92% across the affected routers.
Carlos: No further deploys detected. infra metrics look clean.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert auto-resolved at 12:15 UTC (condition cleared). PagerDuty incident closed automatically.
Jamie: Nice — transient, resolved by cache warmup + local bypass. No further action required. I'll add a short postmortem note in the incident tracker.
Priya: Logging root cause as 'KV prefix cache coldstart after canary join' and action item to add a pre-warm step during canary rollout. Will create ticket INF-249.
Riley: Also suggest we tweak auto-suppression to consider cache-warm windows to avoid noisy pages during scheduled canaries.
Carlos: Filed INF-249 and INF-250 (suppression tuning).
Jamie: Thanks all. Closing thread. :slightly_smiling_face:
